overview: Portmellon is a small sandy cove a mile south of Mevagissey, about a 20-minute walk from the harbour. The beach is around 150 metres long and safe for bathing, but it disappears completely at high tide, so plan around the tide.
At low tide rock pools appear along the edges, and seals are sometimes seen offshore or resting on the rocks. Mevagissey’s first lifeboat station opened here in 1869.

expect.title: Low-tide beach
expect.text: A small sandy beach that’s covered at high water.

expect.title: Rock pools and seals
expect.text: Rock pools appear at low tide, and seals sometimes visit.

expect.title: Slipway
expect.text: A public slipway for launching small boats.

goodToKnow.label: Getting there
goodToKnow.text: A 20-minute walk from Mevagissey, or about six miles south of St Austell by road.

week.slot: An hour or two around low tide
week.text: A nice quiet alternative to Mevagissey’s harbour on a Mevagissey day. Walk out from the village, explore the rock pools at low tide and walk back for lunch.

pairWith.why: the fishing harbour a short walk away
a little aquarium on the harbour

tips: Check the tide times: at high tide there’s no beach at all.
